ops.title: Local task lint reports SA5011s that CI does not — golangci-lint version skew, not baseline debt
ops.body:
`task lint` on a local checkout can report staticcheck SA5011 ("possible nil pointer dereference") at `internal/cli/vcsqueue_test.go:179,182` and `internal/semsearch/index/cache_test.go:22,25`. All four are the ordinary `if got == nil { t.Fatal(...) }` followed by a dereference — the shape staticcheck normally understands, since `t.Fatal` does not return.

CI does not see them. The `lint` job of the CI workflow was green on `main` at df3f2be (run 33706921669), the same commit these files sit at, and it installs its own toolchain via `golangci/golangci-lint-action@v9` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:114`). A local `golangci-lint --version` reports `2.12.2 ... (unknown, modified: ?)` — a locally built or patched binary, not the pinned one.

Do not fix these forward. CI is the gate and it is green; rewriting test code to satisfy a locally-divergent linter is the "don't contort code to satisfy a checker" case in AGENTS.md § General Rules, and it would add scar tissue to files nobody is otherwise touching.

Two things that would change this verdict: `golangci-lint-action@v9` floating onto a version that does flag them (CI goes red on its own, with no commit of ours involved), or the local binary being brought back in line with the pinned one and the findings surviving. Related: the `golangci-max-same-issues` memory — a rule caps at 3 instances per run by default, so a count seen locally is a floor, not a total.

Observed 2026-09-03 while landing the 0.57.0 path-scoped ship fix.
